Body: The backend `GET /config/plugin-settings` response includes `global` and `project` maps, and the PATCH body supports an optional `scope`, but the generated SDK types here don’t include those fields. This indicates the SDK was generated from an outdated OpenAPI spec (or the spec is missing these properties). Regenerate the SDK after updating the spec so `ConfigPluginSettingsGetResponses[200]` includes `global`/`project` and `ConfigPluginSettingsUpdateData.body` includes `scope?: "global" | "project"`.

The backend GET response now includes separate `global` and `project` maps (and PATCH supports `scope`), but the UI response type only models `{schemas, values}` and the UI doesn’t show scope origin/badges or allow saving to global vs project. This is a functional gap vs the PR description (scope-aware UI) and also blocks saving secrets (global-only).

`LegacyConfig.files[].format` advertises support for `yaml` and `toml`, but `parseFile()` doesn’t actually parse those formats (it falls back to `JSON.parse`, which will fail for real YAML/TOML). Either implement real YAML/TOML parsing or restrict the allowed `format` values to what’s supported to avoid surprising migration failures.

For `scope !== "global"` this handler merges against `Config.get()` (the merged config) and then persists via `Config.update(...)`. This risks mixing global values into the project layer (and vice versa), and combined with the current `Config.update()` persistence target it can make project-scope updates not reflect in the merged `values` returned by GET. Use a scope-specific base (`Config.getProject()` for project scope) and persist to a project config source that `Config.get()` actually loads.

The SDK client in `globalSDK.client` is the v2 generated client (`createOpencodeClient`), so `client.config["plugin-settings"].$get/$patch` won’t exist. This will always fall back to `fetch(...)`, but the fallback does not include the server’s Basic auth header, so requests will fail against authenticated servers. Prefer calling the generated methods (e.g., `globalSDK.client.config.pluginSettings.get(...)` / `.update(...)`) so auth + baseUrl are handled consistently, or at least forward the auth header in the fetch fallback.
Could you do `store.mode === "normal"` instead? This way the behaviour will stay explicit if we add any different modes in the future.

`pendingUser` relies solely on `Binary.search` to locate `item.parentID`. In this file you already fall back to a linear search in `messageIndex` when `Binary.search` doesn’t find a match; without a similar fallback here, `pendingUser()` can incorrectly return `undefined` when the message list isn’t strictly sorted, which then breaks `active()`, `working()`, and `queued()` state.

Consider mirroring the `messageIndex` approach: if `Binary.search` returns `found: false`, fall back to `messages.find((m) => m.id === item.parentID)` (or `findIndex`) before returning.
```suggestion
    let msg = result.found ? messages[result.index] : messages.find((m) => m.id === item.parentID)
```

The error message from the server uses the key `error` (e.g. `{ error: "Invalid credentials" }`), but the login page reads `data.message` to display the error. Since the response will never have a `message` property, this will always evaluate to `undefined`, and the displayed error will always be the fallback "Failed to log in" instead of the actual server error message. This should read `data.error` instead of `data.message`.
```suggestion
      setError(data.error || "Failed to log in")
```

The `LoginRoute` is rendered inside `RouterRoot` which wraps all routes in `AppShellProviders > Layout`. The `Layout` component unconditionally calls `useGlobalSDK()` (line 100) and `useGlobalSync()` (line 101), which both throw an error with `"GlobalSDK context must be used within a context provider"` and `"useGlobalSync must be used within GlobalSyncProvider"` respectively when accessed outside their providers. Since `GlobalSDKProvider` and `GlobalSyncProvider` are only set up inside `AuthenticatedGate` (which only wraps the authenticated routes, not `/login`), navigating to the `/login` route will throw a context error and crash the app. The `LoginRoute` must be rendered outside the scope of `RouterRoot`, or a separate router root must be used for the login route that doesn't require these providers.

The `sign` and `verify` functions, as well as `verifySessionCookie`, are exported but appear to be internal implementation details. Exporting `sign` and `verify` unnecessarily expands the public API surface, making them accessible to other modules and harder to change without breaking callers. Only `createSessionCookie`, `verifySessionCookie`, and `dualAuth` are consumed externally (in `server.ts`), so `sign` and `verify` should not be exported.
```suggestion
export { createSessionCookie, verifySessionCookie, dualAuth }
```

The new `auth.ts` module implements security-critical functionality (token signing, verification, and dual-auth middleware) but has no corresponding test coverage. The existing test suite in `packages/opencode/test/server/` tests other server behaviors thoroughly. Tests should be added for at minimum: `sign`/`verify` correctness, `verifySessionCookie` expiry logic, and `dualAuth` middleware behavior (valid cookie, valid Basic Auth, invalid cookie falling through to Basic Auth, and unauthenticated requests).

The intermediate variable `const secret = password` is immediately used in the next line as `verifySessionCookie(cookie, secret)`. This variable serves no purpose since `password` could be passed directly. This is a minor readability issue.
```suggestion
      const sub = await verifySessionCookie(cookie, password)
```

The session cookie is set without the `secure` flag. When the server is accessed over plain HTTP (which is the default), this is acceptable. However, if users configure the server behind an HTTPS proxy or expose it over the network, the cookie will also be transmitted over HTTPS without issues since `secure: true` simply restricts the cookie to HTTPS. For defence-in-depth, consider adding `secure: true` when the server is known to be operating over HTTPS, or document that this is intentionally omitted for HTTP-only deployments.
```suggestion
            maxAge: 86400,
            secure: new URL(c.req.url).protocol === "https:",
```

The `/api/login` endpoint uses `body.username` (from the untrusted request body) to create the session token, even though it has already verified that `body.username === username` (the server-configured value). The token should be created with `username` (the validated server-side variable) rather than the user-supplied `body.username` to make the code's intent clearer and avoid any ambiguity.
```suggestion
          const token = await createSessionCookie(username, password)
```

Auth middleware bypasses authentication for any path ending in `.js/.css/.svg/.png/.ico`. That’s broader than necessary and can accidentally exempt non-static routes if they match those suffixes. Consider limiting the bypass to known static prefixes (e.g. `/assets/`, `/favicon.ico`) rather than extension-based checks.
```suggestion
            path === "/favicon.ico"
```

Token verification compares `expected !== token` using normal string equality. That comparison is not constant-time and can leak information via timing side-channels. Consider using a constant-time compare (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on byte arrays) when comparing signatures/tokens.

Login error handling reads `data.message`, but `/api/login` returns `{ error: string }` on failures. This will cause the UI to always show the fallback message. Align the response shape (client reads `error`, or server returns `message`).
```suggestion
      setError(data.error || "Failed to log in")
```

Session cookie is set without `secure: true`. If the UI is ever served over HTTPS, browsers may still accept a non-secure cookie over HTTP, which is risky. Consider setting `secure` based on request scheme / environment (e.g. only allow non-secure cookies for localhost dev).
```suggestion
            maxAge: 86400,
            secure: new URL(c.req.url).protocol === "https:",
```

`/login` is rendered outside `AuthenticatedGate`, but `RouterRoot` always wraps routes in `Layout` (via `AppShellProviders`), and `Layout` calls `useGlobalSDK()` / `useGlobalSync()`. Without `GlobalSDKProvider`/`GlobalSyncProvider`, navigating to `/login` will throw at runtime. Consider moving `Layout` (and any providers it depends on) under `AuthenticatedGate`, or providing a separate root/layout for the login route that doesn’t require authenticated contexts.
```suggestion
        root={(routerProps) => (
          <AuthenticatedGate>
            <RouterRoot appChildren={props.children}>{routerProps.children}</RouterRoot>
          </AuthenticatedGate>
        )}
      >
        <Route path="/login" component={LoginRoute} />
        <Route path="/" component={HomeRoute} />
        <Route path="/:dir" component={DirectoryLayout}>
          <Route path="/" component={SessionIndexRoute} />
          <Route path="/session/:id?" component={SessionRoute} />
```

This function now unconditionally references `window.location`. This can break non-browser execution (e.g. unit tests, SSR, or worker contexts). Consider guarding with `typeof window !== "undefined"` and defaulting `isSameOrigin` to `false` when `window` is unavailable.

The `status()` check only handles `"idle"` vs. everything else, but `sync.session.status()` can return three distinct values: `"idle"`, `"working"`, and `"compacting"` (when `session.time.compacting` is set). When a subagent's session is compacting, it will display "working" with a warning color, which is misleading because compacting is a distinct background housekeeping operation. The displayed label should reflect the compacting state, and the indicator color could differentiate it (e.g., use a different color or a different label like "compacting").
```suggestion
                              {status() === "idle" ? "idle" : status() === "compacting" ? "compacting" : "working"}
```

`activeSessionID` is module-level state, but requests are scoped to an Instance via the `x-opencode-directory`/`directory` middleware. This means different directories/workspaces handled by the same server process will overwrite each other’s “active session”. If instance scoping matters here, store this value in `Instance.state(...)` (keyed by `Instance.directory`) instead of a module global.

`activeSessionID` is updated before `Bus.publish(...)`. If a subscriber throws during publish, the route will error but `activeSessionID` will still be mutated, leaving server state out of sync with the TUI. To keep state consistent, set `activeSessionID` only after a successful publish (or wrap publish to ensure failures don’t partially apply state).
```suggestion
        await Bus.publish(TuiEvent.SessionSelect, { sessionID })
        activeSessionID = sessionID
```

This POST uses `sdk.fetch` with only a Content-Type header. In HTTP attach mode (and when OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD is set), this request won’t include the Authorization header or x-opencode-directory/workspace headers that the SDK client sends, so reporting will silently fail or be associated with the wrong instance. Please ensure this call uses the same default headers/scoping as other SDK requests (e.g. via a wrapped `sdk.fetch`, or by explicitly merging the SDK provider headers here).
```suggestion
    const defaultHeaders = (sdk as any).headers ?? {}
    sdk
      .fetch(sdk.url + "/tui/active-session", {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { ...defaultHeaders, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
```

The OpenAPI `responses` for this route don’t include validation errors, but `validator("json", ...)` will return a 400 on invalid input. Add `...errors(400)` here so the spec matches runtime behavior (and aligns with other routes in this file that use `validator`).
```suggestion
          },
          ...errors(400),
```

The `InlineTool` `onMouseUp` handler is attached unconditionally (whether or not `onClick` is provided), which means `useRenderer()` is now called in every `InlineTool` instance, even the many that have no `onClick`. More importantly, unlike `BlockTool`, there is no hover visual feedback when `onClick` is present: `BlockTool` changes `backgroundColor` and uses `onMouseOver`/`onMouseOut` signals to highlight the element as clickable. Without this, the Task InlineTool gives the user no visual indication that it is interactive/clickable, making the restored navigation hard to discover. Consider conditionally adding hover state (e.g., `onMouseOver`/`onMouseOut` with a background color change) only when `props.onClick` is defined, to match the `BlockTool` pattern and restore discoverability.

`tooLarge` estimates byte size as `value.length * 2`, which assumes UTF-16 code units and can be misleading for callers passing a true byte limit (e.g., ASCII strings will be treated as 2 bytes/char; surrogate pairs can be 4 bytes/char; and non-localStorage backends may persist as UTF-8). Consider either (a) computing the real byte size via `TextEncoder` (or equivalent) for a consistent definition of “bytes”, or (b) renaming/documenting the option as an approximate UTF-16/memory-size limit so `maxBytes` can be tuned correctly.
```suggestion
  const byteLength = new TextEncoder().encode(value).length
  return byteLength > maxBytes
```
There defaults are just initial values that empirically worked in my testing, and I am open to changing them.

`SessionMessage` duplicates the SDK `Message` / `AssistantMessage` shapes but makes several required fields optional (e.g., `time`, `error.name`, `parentID`). This increases the chance of drifting from the real message contract and forces extra defensive typing inside helpers like `isAbortedAssistant`. Consider importing and using the SDK `Message` types directly and only picking the fields you need (e.g., via `Pick<...>`), so the helper stays aligned with the actual store data.
Going ahead and removing this for now until we actually have syncing

`read()` treats WSL as Windows (`os === "win32" || release().includes("WSL")`), but `getCopyMethod()` only checks `os === "win32"`. As a result, this new WinRT clipboard path will never be used from WSL. If WSL copy support is intended to mirror `read()`, consider adding the same `release().includes("WSL")` condition here (or documenting why copy differs).
```suggestion
    if (os === "win32" || release().includes("WSL")) {
```

When `busy` is `true` (a streaming request is in flight on the existing `ws` connection) and a new request arrives, the `open()` function falls through all three early-return guards and creates a brand-new WebSocket connection. This means that if a second concurrent request comes in while the first is still streaming, a second parallel connection is established and both requests can proceed simultaneously on separate sockets. This is likely unintentional for a design that assumes a single shared connection, and it bypasses the concurrency protection that `busy` is supposed to provide.

The new `openai-websocket-fetch.ts` module contains non-trivial state management (`busy`, `ws`, `con`, `sig`), fallback logic, SSE-over-WebSocket bridging, and abort handling — but has no automated tests. The existing provider test suite (e.g., `test/provider/provider.test.ts`) provides extensive coverage for similar logic. Tests covering at least: successful streaming, WebSocket connection reuse, fallback to HTTP, abort handling, and the `response.completed`/`response.incomplete` terminal event logic would reduce the risk of regressions.

The German translation for `common.unarchive` is misspelled as "Darchivieren". Please correct this string (e.g., "De-archivieren" / "Entarchivieren" depending on the desired phrasing) so the UI doesn’t display an incorrect label.
```suggestion
  "common.unarchive": "Entarchivieren",
```

PR description says to use the command palette entry "Browse unarchived sessions", but the command added here is "Browse archived sessions" (`command.session.browseArchived`). Please align the user-facing name in the PR description (or, if the code is intended to browse *unarchived* sessions, adjust the command/translation keys accordingly).

`Session.setArchived` now coalesces `undefined` to `null` via `input.time ?? null`. Since `time` is optional in the schema, any caller that forgets to pass `time` will unintentionally *unarchive* the session. Consider either (a) making `time` required (but nullable) in the schema, or (b) keeping it optional but passing `input.time` through directly so `undefined` doesn’t clear the column.
```suggestion
          .set({ time_archived: input.time })
```

This new table row isn’t formatted consistently with the rest of the Markdown table (column spacing/alignment around the `|` separators). Running the repo’s Prettier formatting on this file should reflow it to match the existing rows and reduce noisy diffs in future edits.
```suggestion
| [opencode-loamlog](https://github.com/tongsh6/loamlog/tree/master/plugins/opencode)                       | Capture every OpenCode session on idle and archive as structured JSON snapshots via the loam daemon |
```

Would it make sense to change the wording here, to hint to the LLM that this isn't a live updating value? Otherwise it might make some weird choices elsewhere for long lived conversations. E.g.

```suggestion
        `  Session started at: ${date.toDateString()}`,
```

On Windows, returning the bare string "pwsh"/"powershell" here can break downstream logic that assumes shells ending with "sh" are POSIX shells (e.g. `Pty.create()` appends `-l` when `command.endsWith("sh")`, which matches `pwsh`). Consider returning the resolved executable path from `Bun.which(...)` (typically ends with `.exe`) or otherwise ensuring the returned value won’t match that heuristic; also consider de-duplicating the pwsh/powershell selection logic between `preferred` and `acceptable` to avoid drift.

This PR changes Windows shell selection behavior (pwsh/powershell preference and updated blacklist logic), but there are no unit tests covering `Shell.preferred()` / `Shell.acceptable()` on win32 or the interaction with call sites like `Pty.create()`. Adding targeted tests (with platform/env/which stubbing) would help prevent regressions like incorrect args being appended or blacklisted shells slipping through.

This still hardcodes "opencode", so run --attach will keep failing against servers using a non-default OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME. Can we read the username from env here (like worker.ts) instead of only fixing the password path?

Timeout handling in `KaliTool.execute` is currently ineffective: an `AbortController` is created but never passed to anything, and `kali.exec()` has no way to be aborted. Also, the `catch` block treats any thrown error as a timeout and returns exitCode 124, which would mask real failures (e.g., Docker errors). Implement an actual timeout (e.g., `docker exec ...` via `$().timeout(...)` / `AbortSignal` support, or run `docker exec` in a child process you can kill), and only mark `timedOut=true` when the timeout triggers.

The GitLab webhook endpoint is behind the global `basicAuth` middleware. If `OPENSACIA_SERVER_PASSWORD` is set, GitLab webhooks will receive 401 unless GitLab is configured with Basic Auth credentials (which is uncommon). Consider exempting `/hooks/gitlab/*` from basic auth (or documenting/enforcing a different auth mechanism for webhooks).

`handleGitLabWebhook` only checks that `X-Gitlab-Token` is present, but does not validate it against a configured shared secret. This allows anyone to POST arbitrary events to the endpoint as long as they include any token value. Add a configured webhook secret (env/config) and compare it in constant time, returning 401/403 when it doesn't match.

`GitLabProvider` uses `@octokit/rest` with `auth: config.token`, which results in a GitHub-style `Authorization: token ...` header. GitLab's API expects `PRIVATE-TOKEN: ...` (PAT) or `Authorization: Bearer ...`; the current setup is likely to authenticate incorrectly and break all GitLab API calls. Consider switching to a GitLab client (e.g. `@gitbeaker/node`) or a small `fetch` wrapper that sets the correct headers and reuses `retryWithBackoff`.

Root `package.json` pins `react` to 19.2.4, while `packages/storybook/package.json` pins `react` to 18.2.0 (and `@types/react` 18.x). This will likely produce multiple React versions in the workspace and can cause Storybook/JSX-email peer dependency mismatches. Consider aligning versions across the workspace (or keeping React scoped to the packages that need it) to avoid duplication and compatibility issues.
```suggestion
    "react": "18.2.0",
```

The new static asset handler uses `serveStatic` directly for all unmatched paths. Since the web app uses `@solidjs/router` with nested routes (e.g. `/:dir/session/:id?`), deep links will request non-file paths and likely 404. Consider adding an SPA fallback that serves `index.html` for unknown paths (while still letting API routes take precedence).

The static file serving path removed the previous response hardening (e.g. Content-Security-Policy that was previously set on proxied responses). If you still need CSP/other security headers for the web UI, consider adding middleware to set them on static responses as well.

The function comment says it "only process MR note events", but the filter currently only rejects non-MR note events; `merge_request` webhook payloads will still return `shouldProcess: true`. Either tighten the filter to match the intended behavior or update the comment/return value contract so downstream processing can handle other event kinds safely.

`mapEventType()` maps `objectKind === "discussion"` to type `"note"`, even though `WebhookEvent["type"]` includes a distinct `"discussion"` value and the GitHub provider emits it. This loses information and makes consumers handle `discussion` events inconsistently across providers; consider returning `"discussion"` when appropriate.

`checkoutMR()` does `git fetch origin ${branch}` followed by `git checkout ${branch}`. If the branch doesn’t exist locally yet, `git checkout <branch>` can fail unless Git auto-tracking is configured. Consider checking out from the remote explicitly (e.g., create/reset a local branch tracking `origin/<branch>`), similar to how fork PR handling was done previously.

`fullCommand` is built as a single string and passed down to `KaliContainer.exec()`. Given the current `exec()` implementation escapes interpolated strings, this will break any command with arguments. Prefer keeping `command`/`args` as structured values and passing them as separate argv segments (or executing through `sh -lc`).

When falling back to parsing `file.diff` to compute additions/deletions, lines like `+++ b/file` and `--- a/file` will be counted as additions/deletions, inflating totals. If you need this fallback, filter out diff headers (e.g., ignore `+++`/`---`/`@@` lines) before counting.

Two tests use `fetch("http://invalid:9999/..." )` and `fetch("http://localhost:11434/invalid")` without any timeout/AbortSignal. Depending on DNS/network settings this can hang or slow CI significantly. Consider adding an `AbortController` with a short timeout (similar to the first test) or fully mocking `fetch` for these cases.

`exec()` passes the entire `command` string as a single escaped argument to `docker exec`. With Bun's `$` template interpolation, spaces are quoted/escaped, so commands like `nmap -sV ...` or `echo 'hi'` will be treated as one argv and will fail to execute inside the container. Consider executing via a shell (`docker exec <id> sh -lc <command>`) or changing the API to accept `{cmd, args[]}` and pass them as separate template segments.

`createPersistent(name)` uses `name` directly as the Docker container name. In `KaliTool` this is currently called with `params.command`, which can include invalid characters/whitespace and will also collide across runs (e.g. multiple persistent `nmap` containers). Prefer generating a unique/sanitized ID (similar to `generateId()`) and keep the tool name separately for display/logging.

`tmpdir()` calls `options.init` with `dirpath`, but later calls `options.dispose` with `realpath` (and returns `path: realpath`). This mismatch can break callers that assume the same directory string is used throughout the fixture lifecycle. Consider resolving `realpath` immediately after `mkdir` and then using that resolved path consistently for git init/config, `init`, returned `path`, and `dispose` (or pass both explicitly).

**`brew tap` failure silently swallowed, changing upgrade semantics**

The old shell chain was:
```
brew tap anomalyco/tap && cd "$(brew --repo anomalyco/tap)" && git pull --ff-only && brew upgrade ${formula}
```

Because of the `&&` operators, any step failure caused the entire command to exit non-zero, and with `.throws(false)` the `result.exitCode !== 0` check would then throw `UpgradeFailedError`.

In the new code, `brew tap anomalyco/tap` runs with `nothrow: true` and its result is never checked. If tapping fails (e.g. network error), execution continues and `brew upgrade` is attempted anyway. In many cases this produces a misleading "upgrade succeeded" result when the tap is actually stale.

Consider checking the tap result and surfacing the error:
```ts
const tap = await Process.run(["brew", "tap", "anomalyco/tap"], { env, nothrow: true })
const repo = tap.code === 0
  ? (await Process.text(["brew", "--repo", "anomalyco/tap"], { env, nothrow: true })).text.trim()
  : ""
if (repo) await Process.run(["git", "pull", "--ff-only"], { cwd: repo, env, nothrow: true })
result = tap.code === 0
  ? await Process.run(["brew", "upgrade", formula], { env, nothrow: true })
  : tap
```

**`result` variable lacks an explicit type**

`let result` is untyped, and the branches assign either the object returned by `upgradeCurl` (`{ code: number, stdout: Buffer, stderr: Buffer }`) or `Process.Result` from `Process.run()`. While both shapes are compatible for the checks below, the implicit `any`-like widening makes it harder to catch future mismatches at compile time.

Consider annotating it:
```suggestion
    let result: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof upgradeCurl>> | undefined
```
Or simply `let result: { code: number; stdout: Buffer; stderr: Buffer } | undefined` to be explicit.

**`TextResult.text` (property) vs `GitResult.text()` (method) — inconsistent API surface across the codebase**

`Process.text()` returns `TextResult` where `text` is a plain `string` property, while `util/git.ts` returns `GitResult` where `text` is a zero-arg method (`text()`). This means callers accessing stdout text must choose between `result.text` and `result.text()` depending on which helper they used. The mixed surface makes it easy to accidentally call `result.text` as a property when the caller is holding a `GitResult` (getting the function reference rather than the string), or vice-versa.

Consider aligning the two shapes — either both expose `text` as a property, or both expose it as a method — to make the API uniform across the codebase. Since `GitResult` appears in the older helper and the majority of call sites, making `TextResult.text` a method (or aliasing both) would be the least disruptive change.

`Process.text()` / `Process.lines()` are newly added but there are no unit tests covering them (including behavior when `nothrow` is set and the command fails). This change switches from streaming line iteration (previously `for await (...)` over Bun’s `.lines()`) to `await Process.lines(...)`, which buffers the entire command output into memory before processing. For large diffs, this can increase peak memory and delay first-item processing. Consider using a streaming approach (e.g., spawn + readline) or adding a `Process.iterLines()` async iterator helper to preserve the previous behavior.

Both `Process.run` calls use default options (no `nothrow: true`), so a non-zero exit from `powershell` or `unzip` will throw a `RunFailedError`. The original Bun `$` calls also lacked `.nothrow()`, so the throwing behaviour is unchanged — however, one call site (`lsp/server.ts`) catches the error via `.catch()` while other call sites (also in `lsp/server.ts`) do not. Worth verifying all callers intentionally tolerate exceptions from this function.

`OPENCODE_VERSION` is read into `version` and then used to build download URLs (via `v${version}`), but earlier in this script the guard mistakenly checks `releaseId` a second time instead of validating `version`. If `OPENCODE_VERSION` is unset, this will silently generate `vundefined` URLs for all targets (including the new Windows arm64 entry). Update the env var validation to throw when `version` is missing.

This can produce misleading messages (e.g., when `target` is passed explicitly or when the env var is unset). Use the `target` parameter in the error message (and the initial guard) so the failure accurately reports which Rust target was requested.

This test relies on very small real-time delays (5ms) to ensure `time.updated` differs and that `Session.list` sorts deterministically.
